title.narrative: Humanitarian Support: Improving Humanitarian Action - Egypt Flexible Funds (Gaza response)

description.narrative: Humanitarian support (Flexible Funds): Outcomes for crisis-affected populations are improved through agile, efficient and effective humanitarian assistance with identified strategic and emergent priorities: This response combines mental health and psychosocial support, multi-purpose cash assistance, and efforts to strengthen education inclusion for Palestinian children displaced to Egypt. Through child-friendly spaces and caregiver support zones in hospitals and shelters, SC delivers trauma-informed group and individual sessions, alongside 400 mental health and psychosocial support kits as well as specialised skills-development support for children with disabilities, including individualized assessments, care plans and family guidance. Caregivers participate in structured support groups based on SC’s Safe Families methodology, with referrals to specialised services for severe cases. To help families meet basic needs with dignity, SC provides three months of multi-purpose cash assistance to around 950 evacuees, using flexible delivery mechanisms such as prepaid cards and SMS transfers, aligned with the national survival minimum expenditure basket. Cash recipients are linked to additional services and supported through post-distribution monitoring. Recognising the increasingly protracted nature of displacement, SC also engages in education advocacy with the government to support Palestinian children’s access to public schools and strengthens social inclusion through child-led dialogues. Thirty Palestinian and Egyptian children will participate in a four-day interactive event addressing violence, well-being and inclusion, culminating in child-generated recommendations for national authorities, with safeguarding as well as mental health and psychosocial support throughout. All SC programmes are gender mainstreamed, inclusive and aims to strengthen resilience.
